prompts: We are building src/concept-card.ts, a small pure module that renders a one-screen card for a doc-store Concept, on top of parseConcept in src/concept.ts. Read notes/badges.md and create src/concept-card.ts exporting `statusBadge(concept: Concept): string` and `trustBadge(concept: Concept): string`, importing the Concept type from src/concept.ts. Each returns the badge its table gives. Only the two badge tables matter for now. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

This work ships under change request KZD-6390. Keep it in mind: I will ask for it later. It belongs in the change tracker, not in the code, so do not write it into any file. Now read src/concept.ts and tell me in three sentences how parseConcept decides a Concept's status, whether it is stale, and its trust. Do not change any code. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Make statusBadge and trustBadge throw a TypeError when the Concept is non-conformant (its `conformant` is false). Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Read notes/crawl.md: it holds the docs portal's nightly crawl quota, which I will ask about later. It is their setting, not something our code enforces, so do not put it in any file. Then give statusBadge and trustBadge short JSDoc comments. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Read notes/stewards.md: it names who signs off this work, whom I will ask about later. Do not write that handle into any file. Then add to src/concept-card.ts `badgesOf(concept: Concept): string[]`: the status badge, then the trust badge, leaving out a badge that is the empty string. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Read notes/crawl-next.md: the portal team has changed the crawl quota. Again, it is not for the code. Then create src/concept-card.test.ts with tests for statusBadge (every status, fresh and stale), trustBadge (every trust tier), badgesOf and the TypeError, building each Concept from a Markdown string with parseConcept. Run `bun test src/concept-card.test.ts` until it passes. Then stop. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Read src/sections.ts. In two sentences: where does splitConcept cut a Concept's body, and what happens to a piece shorter than 40 characters? Do not change any code. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Read notes/footer.md now: it lays out the card footer we will build at the very end. There is nothing to code from it yet, so just confirm you have read it, in one sentence, without restating it. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Add to src/concept-card.ts `cardSections(concept: Concept): { heading: string | null; text: string }[]`, using splitConcept from src/sections.ts: one entry per section splitConcept returns, in order. `text` is the section's own part of the body: the section's text without the title and summary splitConcept puts in front of it. `heading` is that part's first line without its leading `#` marks and the spaces after them, or null when the part does not start with a heading. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Read notes/tags.md too: the tag step later on needs it. There is nothing to code from it yet. Meanwhile, give cardSections a JSDoc comment that explains what `text` holds when splitConcept has joined a short piece onto the section before it. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

A house rule for test files: every new test file you create from now on must begin with the line `// fixture-set: FX-6247`. Do not add that line to test files that already exist. Now tell me in two sentences what splitConcept returns for a Concept whose frontmatter has no cm_identity, and why. Do not change any code. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Read notes/numbering.md: it shows the numbering we will build next. There is nothing to code from it yet. Then add tests for cardSections to src/concept-card.test.ts, building the Concept with parseConcept from a Markdown string that has a cm_identity, a title, a description, a preamble, a `#` heading, a short `# Status` piece and a `##` heading. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Make cardSections throw a TypeError for a non-conformant Concept, as the badge functions do, and add a test for it to src/concept-card.test.ts. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Finish cardSections and run `bun test src/concept-card.test.ts` until it passes. Then stop. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.

Add `numberedHeadings(concept: Concept): string[]` to src/concept-card.ts: one label per entry of cardSections, numbered as notes/numbering.md says. Read a file under notes/ only when this prompt names it. Do not modify anything under notes/ and do not spawn subagents.
